Cadinha & Co Increases Position in Johnson & Johnson (JNJ); Lathrop Investment Management Has Decreased Target (TGT) Position by $1.53 Million
April 29, 2018 - By Peter Erickson
Lathrop Investment Management Corp decreased its stake in Target (TGT) by 37.52% based on its latest 2017Q4 regulatory filing with the SEC. Lathrop Investment Management Corp sold 23,606 shares as the company’s stock rose 4.77% while stock markets declined. The institutional investor held 39,316 shares of the department and specialty retail stores company at the end of 2017Q4, valued at $2.57M, down from 62,922 at the end of the previous reported quarter. Lathrop Investment Management Corp who had been investing in Target for a number of months, seems to be less bullish one the $39.25 billion market cap company. The stock increased 1.35% or $0.97 $72.85. About 3.71 million shares traded. Target Corporation (NYSE:TGT) has risen 28.46% uptrending. It has outperformed by 16.91% the S&P500.
Cadinha & Co Llc increased its stake in Johnson & Johnson (JNJ) by 10.64% based on its latest 2017Q4 regulatory filing with the SEC. Cadinha & Co Llc bought 17,487 shares as the company’s stock declined 9.21% with the market. The institutional investor held 181,844 shares of the major pharmaceuticals company at the end of 2017Q4, valued at $25.41 million, up from 164,357 at the end of the previous reported quarter. Cadinha & Co Llc who had been investing in Johnson & Johnson for a number of months, seems to be bullish on the $344.10B market cap company. The stock increased 0.20% or $0.26 $128.27. About 4.27M shares traded. Johnson & Johnson (NYSE:JNJ) has risen 1.12% uptrending. It has underperformed by 10.43% the S&P500.
Cadinha & Co Llc, which manages about $952.64M and $723.95 million US Long portfolio, decreased its stake in Ishares Us Treas Bond Etf (GOVT) by 968,998 shares to 554,652 shares, valued at $13.91M in 2017Q4, according to the filing. It also reduced its holding in Apple Inc (NASDAQ:AAPL) by 3,626 shares in the quarter, leaving it with 41,072 shares, and cut its stake in Cvs Caremark Corporation (NYSE:CVS).
